The ED found evidence linking money from the scam to his company, Leaps and Bounds Pvt Ltd.  The **CID** had also issued a notice to **Abhishek Banerjee** for questioning on June 1 regarding a signature forgery case filed by two TMC MLAs who alleged fabricated resolutions.

recent_articles.title: Malviya Nagar Fire Flourish Stay 8 Of A Family Visiting Ailing Relative Killed In Delhi Hotel Fire
recent_articles.rephrased_article: An early morning fire at a bed and breakfast in Malviya Nagar, South Delhi, tragically claimed the lives of eight members of a family. **Vivek Agarwal**, a chartered accountant from Gurugram, had traveled to Delhi to visit his father who is currently receiving treatment at Max Hospital.  The fire broke out while the family was having breakfast in the hotel's restaurant and all eight perished. The only survivor is Vivek’s 80-year-old father, **Radhe Shyam Agarwal**. Authorities are investigating the cause of the fire.

recent_articles.title: CID arrests two in methanol supply chain in hooch tragedy, 20 deaths confirmed | Pune News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Maharashtra Criminal Investigation Department (CID)** has arrested a father-son duo, Arun Jagdamb Choubey and Abhishek Arun Choubey, who owned the company Rex International in Bhiwandi. The pair are suspected of supplying methanol to key accused Yogesh Ramchandra Vhankade, who allegedly mixed it with illicit liquor, leading to 20 deaths in Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad.  The arrests bring the total number of individuals in CID custody to eight. The investigation is ongoing.

recent_articles.title: Pseudo-police gang that kidnapped businessman and extorted ₹5.26 lakh busted in Cyberabad - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Cyberabad police** arrested five members of a pseudo-police gang who allegedly kidnapped a businessman, impersonated police officers, and extorted over ₹5 lakh from him. The suspects, identified as Nagaraju Raghu Varma, Yeswanth Singh alias Rahul, Sathyabhan Singh alias Thakur, Thangellapalli Nagendra Varma, and two others still at large, were apprehended following an investigation into the incident reported by a 42-year-old businessman in Kukatpally. The gang used fake police uniforms, forged identity cards, and other tactics to deceive their victims before withdrawing money from his bank accounts and assaulting him.  Police are continuing to investigate and identify additional victims.

recent_articles.title: 2025 murder of gold merchant: HC asks DGP to take action against absconding BDO, orders action against investigation officer | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court ordered the West Bengal Director General of Police to take action against **absconding** Block Development Officer Prashant Barman, who is accused in the murder of gold merchant Swapan Kamila.  The court also directed disciplinary proceedings against the investigating officer, Saswata Banerjee, for failing to uphold his duty. The court rejected the bail application of Trinamool leader Sajal Sarkar and ordered immediate action against Barman, who has been evading arrest despite a Supreme Court order.

recent_articles.title: TMC leader Jay Prakash Majumdar held over ‘grabbing’ woman’s house | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jay Prakash Majumdar**, a **TMC** leader, was arrested by the police in connection with allegedly illegally occupying a woman's house for several years and harassing her.  The arrest followed a protest against Majumdar outside his flat in Bidhannagar, where he allegedly assaulted some protesters. Meanwhile, Kolkata Police arrested Ward No 42 Councilor **Mahesh Kumar Sharma** on Wednesday in connection with a case filed in 2025.

recent_articles.title: Surat bus crash: Kin provide blood samples for DNA matching | Ahmedabad News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following a head-on collision between two buses near Bardoli town in Gujarat's Surat district, seven people were killed and several injured.  **Ghanshyam Raju Barkale**, the driver of the bus that caught fire, has been identified. The **Bardoli rural police** are facing challenges identifying the deceased due to severe burns. DNA tests have been ordered for relatives of missing passengers, including Sachin Patil whose mother Manisha was on board.  The accident occurred when a Maharashtra State Transport bus jumped the road divider and collided with the other bus.

recent_articles.title: California techie living in $35 million mansion arrested for supplying sensitive US equipment to Iran’s military, faces up to 20 years - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jamshid Ghomi**, a 63-year-old dual Iranian-American national, was arrested at his Newport Beach mansion for allegedly supplying advanced US networking and encryption equipment to Iran's nuclear and military institutions for over a decade.  The **US justice department** alleges that he used middlemen in the UAE to route purchases and shipments through eBay and PayPal between 2011 and 2015, smuggling over 250 metric tonnes of equipment into Iran between 2014 and 2018. Ghomi's company, Faraz Pardaz Rayaneh (FPR), generated over $10 million in annual sales and supplied the Iranian defense ministry and nuclear agency between 2014 and 2023. Prosecutors claim he moved over $15 million from Iran into US accounts falsely described as foreign inheritance, which was laundered through shell companies in various locations.

recent_articles.title: How Pune IT firm duped nearly 700 techies before vanishing | Pune News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **ThynkTech India OPC Pvt Ltd**, a tech start-up that recruited hundreds of engineering graduates across Maharashtra, abruptly shut down its Hinjewadi office in Pune. The company's CEO, Harshal Thakre, disappeared and failed to pay rent, maintenance charges, and electricity bills, leading to the sealing of the office.  **ThynkTech India** promised internships and job opportunities with a monthly stipend and a confirmed salary upon completion of training. However, interns were left without laptops, training, or compensation after discovering that the company was not legitimate. **ThynkTech India** has been accused of fraud by affected interns who are demanding action against the CEO and the clearing of all outstanding payments.
